Tina (Support): FYI BrightSource reported a burst of 5xx + long timeouts hitting hosted inference in us-west2 starting ~08:40 PST. Customer sees retry loops in their app and rising token usage. Can we triage?
Alex R: Can you paste their SDK version, region, and a minimal repro?
Tina (Support): SDK: go-redwood v0.8.1, region us-west2. Large prompts (~3.2MB) used for batch generate. Pattern: 502 -> 504 -> SDK retries -> client concurrency ramps -> more 5xx. Thread/root ts 3251234567.
Maria G: Oncall bot flagged a gateway surge at 08:42. Initial glance shows ingress-hosted-usw2 502 spike and concurrent connections jumped to ~2.2k. Might be kvcache eviction/lock pressure on long sequences.
Sam L: Can you drop the exact request + their client config so I can try to repro?
Tina (Support): Here's sample curl and snippet they used: 
```bash
curl -X POST "https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate" \
 -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" \
 -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
 -d '{"model":"rw-large","input":"<large prompt...>", "stream": false, "max_tokens": 1024}'
```
and their SDK usage: 
```go
client := redwood.NewClient(opts.WithRegion("us-west2"), opts.WithTimeout(15*time.Second))
resp, err := client.Generate(ctx, req)
```
Sam L: Noted they set timeout=15s and have aggressive retry/concurrency. That can create hysteresis at the gateway when upstream queues slow.
eng-oncall-bot: INC-20250324-1428 created for hosted-usw2 5xx spike.
Alex R: I'm going to pull serving runtime logs for kv-cache hold times and check GPU queue depth. Maria, can you check LB/HAProxy for upstream resets and write errors?
Maria G: On it. Early logs show repeated "backend reset" and "upstream write failure". Kv-cache eviction rate increased coincident with spike. Sample line: "upstream write error: write tcp 10.0.0.12:443->10.0.1.5:52000: write: connection reset by peer"
Tina (Support): Customer asked for immediate mitigation suggestions — they want something quick to stop billing surge and 5xx in prod.
Sam L: Quick customer guidance: set client max_concurrency to 4, add exponential backoff with jitter, and temporarily disable aggressive retry bursts. That reduces pressure on the gateway. I'll draft message.
Alex R: I found a hotpath: for very long kv sequences we hold the kvcache lock longer than expected which serializes large generate calls. I can roll a small runtime patch to reduce lock hold time and push a canary to a small pool. ETA 15m.
eng-oncall-bot: DEPLOY CANARY: runtime v2.8.1-hotfix-kvcache -> canary group 'canary-kvcache-1' started.
Tina (Support): Sent mitigation steps to BrightSource; they applied client-side changes (limit concurrency + jitter). They report 5xxs dropped within ~10m and p95 latency improved. Still seeing occasional 502s but much better.
Sam L: We'll keep monitors on p95 and 5xx rate. Propose alert: hosted-usw2 5xx rate >0.5% sustained for 10m. Also track token-billing deltas when retry storms occur.
Alex R: Postmortem/action items: 1) ship kvcache lock reduction fix to stable 2) update SDK default retry policy to include jitter and sensible concurrency limits for large payloads 3) add instrumentation for kvcache hold time per request 4) add docs guidance for large-prompt best practices and recommended client settings 5) run a small chaos test for kv eviction scenarios.
Maria G: I'll attach the relevant LB and kvcache graphs to the incident and set retention on logs for deeper analysis.
Tina (Support): Drafting final customer comms: explained root cause hypothesis (kvcache lock/ingress pressure) + what we changed and what they changed client-side, and next steps. Will close the loop once stable for 2 hours. :thumbsup:
Alex R: Thanks. If we see any regression after canary -> rollout, we'll pause and revert.
Tina (Support): BrightSource confirms stable -> closing on customer side, leaving incident open for internal follow-ups.
